**About Signant Health**

At Signant Health, we help bring life-changing treatments to patients faster. We are a global evidence generation company that supports clinical trials with smart technology, scientific expertise, and hands-on operational support — so better data leads to better decisions in healthcare. We embrace AI and advanced technologies to enhance every aspect of what we do, from data analysis to operational efficiency.

Our teams work at the intersection of science, technology, and patient experience, delivering digital solutions powered by AI innovation that make clinical trials more efficient, more accurate, and more accessible around the world. Trusted by leading pharmaceutical companies and CROs, our platforms and services support studies across more than 90 countries and have contributed to hundreds of new drug approvals.

If you are motivated by meaningful work, global impact, and innovation in clinical research and digital health — including the opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI technologies — you will find purpose and opportunity at Signant Health.

**About The Role**

Signant Health is looking for a Software Engineer – AI Accelerated Development to build AI-powered, agentic features into our clinical trial platforms. Working across the .NET stack, you will take AI capabilities from backend LLM integration through to a usable front-end — designing agents and agentic workflows, not just prompting a model. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who works with agentic tooling every day and wants to ship production AI in a regulated, high-impact environment. We weigh the depth of your AI and agentic build experience more heavily than years of general experience: a developer with one to three years of substantive, hands-on agentic work is exactly the profile we are targeting.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES – Function**

* Design and build AI agents and agentic workflows — tool-use/function calling, multi-step task orchestration, and agent loops — that power Signant Health's clinical trial platforms.
* Integrate LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, or Azure OpenAI) into .NET application code, handling authentication, streaming, error handling, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
* Deliver AI features end-to-end, taking them from backend integration through to a usable, production-ready front-end.
* Build custom agents and tools with the Claude Agent SDK, wiring and steering agent loops.
* Author custom skills and slash commands for Claude Code to codify team-specific workflows.
* Implement RAG pipelines and integrate vector stores (e.g. Qdrant, pgvector, Pinecone) to ground agent outputs in trusted data.
* Instrument agents for evaluation and observability so their outputs can be verified, measured, and audited.
* Apply AI-specific risk controls appropriate to a regulated clinical environment, addressing hallucination, determinism, and auditability of agent decisions.
* Use Claude Code (or an equivalent agentic CLI) daily as a primary development tool, reviewing and steering AI-generated diffs.

**Knowledge, Skills & Attributes**

**Essential:**

* Full-stack .NET development — C#/ASP.NET Core on the backend paired with a modern front-end framework.
* Hands-on agentic development experience — building AI agents or agentic workflows (tool-use/function calling, multi-step task orchestration, agent loops); not just prompting an LLM, but building systems around one.
* Practical LLM API integration (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, or Azure OpenAI), including authentication, streaming, error handling, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
* Proven full-stack delivery of AI features — able to take an agentic/AI feature from backend integration through to a usable front-end, not just a notebook prototype.
* Daily, hands-on use of Claude Code (or an equivalent agentic CLI) as a primary development tool — comfortable working through multi-step agentic sessions and reviewing and steering AI-generated diffs, rather than occasional autocomplete-style use.
* Prompt engineering — designing and iterating on system prompts as production software contracts, not one-off experiments.
* Python proficiency as the preferred language for AI/agent tooling; comfort with async patterns a plus.
* Evaluation and observability literacy — able to reason about whether an agent's output is correct and instrument it to prove so.

**Desirable:**

* Claude Agent SDK experience — building custom agents, defining tools, and wiring agent loops.
* Working knowledge of agent primitives: hooks (deterministic pre/post-tool-call controls), skills (progressive-disclosure, load-on-demand instructions), subagents/multi-agent delegation, and session/state management.
* Experience authoring custom skills or slash commands for Claude Code to codify team-specific workflows.
* Exposure to MCP (Model Context Protocol) for connecting agents to internal tools and data sources.
* Working knowledge of RAG patterns and vector store integration (e.g. Qdrant, pgvector, Pinecone).
* Awareness of AI-specific risk areas relevant to a regulated environment (OWASP LLM Top 10, hallucination/determinism concerns, and auditability of agent decisions).

At Signant Health, your work has real impact. Everything we build, support, and deliver helps advance clinical research and bring new treatments to patients faster — improving lives around the world. Our teams combine science, technology, and operational expertise to solve complex clinical trial challenges, and every role contributes to that mission.

**About The Team**
The Post-Training team advances OpenAI’s frontier models and prepares them for deployment in ChatGPT, Codex, the API, and future products. We work at the intersection of research and product to make models more capable, useful, safe, and reliable for millions of users.
  
  
We define the capabilities our models should have, build the training signals that teach those abilities, and run the experiments that make them real. Our work spans reinforcement learning, model behavior and alignment, reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities such as tool use, computer use, and long-horizon execution. We build the data, environments, evaluations, and training methods that shape model behavior, then carry those improvements through major training runs and into the products people use.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Research Engineer / Research Scientist on Post-Training, you will research and develop improvements to the capabilities, reliability, and real-world performance of OpenAI’s models. You might own a research direction, develop new training methods, build infrastructure for large-scale experiments, or create evaluations that reveal where models fail. You will take ideas from early experimentation through integration and deployment.
  
  
We’re looking for people with strong machine learning engineering skills and research experience who are excited about product-driven research. This role is intentionally broad: you should be comfortable taking an ambiguous problem and making progress across research, engineering, data, and evaluations. You will collaborate closely with researchers, product and infrastructure teams, and safety and alignment partners to translate user needs into model improvements and help determine what is ready for major model runs.
  
  
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
  
  
**In this role, you might**

* Own and pursue a research agenda to improve model capabilities, behavior, and performance, from defining hypotheses and running experiments to analyzing results and shipping improvements.
* Develop and improve post-training methods and systems, including reinforcement learning, data mixtures, synthetic data, reward signals, graders, and training pipelines.
* Build robust evaluations and environments that measure progress, expose model failures, and turn those findings into better training data, methods, and product experiences.
* Design, implement, test, and debug code across the research stack, improving the reliability, efficiency, observability, and reproducibility of large-scale experiments.
* Collaborate with research and product teams across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API to understand user needs and translate real-world feedback into model improvements.
* Advance capabilities such as reasoning, factuality, instruction following, coding, tool use, and long-horizon task execution, with opportunities to work on computer use and multi-agent collaboration.
* Partner with safety and alignment teams to develop useful, reliable model behavior and evaluate readiness for deployment.

**You might thrive in this role if you**

* Have strong fundamentals in machine learning and software engineering, with research or applied experience developing and improving machine learning models.
* Have hands-on experience in one or more relevant areas, such as large language models, reinforcement learning, RLHF/RLAIF, post-training, evaluations, synthetic data, agentic systems, or production ML systems.
* Can turn an ambiguous model-behavior problem into a concrete experiment: define the hypothesis, build the pipeline, run the model, analyze the results, and decide what to do next.
* Are comfortable navigating and debugging a large ML codebase and building dependable systems that support research at scale.
* Care about product impact and how models behave in practice, including what makes them useful, reliable, honest, and easy to work with.
* Thrive in a dynamic, technically complex environment where the path is unclear and progress requires both research judgment and engineering execution.
* Communicate clearly and collaborate across research, product, infrastructure, data, evaluations, and safety teams.

Job Description

Purified tap water, food and beverage production, massive data centers, and advanced manufacturing facilities all depend on industrial software that can't go down. As a Software Solutions Engineer I, you'll be the person customers call when something breaks, working through root causes with them in real time. Whether your background is in Computer Science or Electrical Engineering/Controls, you’ll help bridge Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT). 



You’ll like this job if: 

You love connecting the dots between a timestamp, a cryptic error message, and a weird software behavior. You see a complex failure as a puzzle, and you won't walk away until you find the root cause. You're also patient and warm with people, even when they're stressed.  You like working as part of a team with both colleagues and customers, in an environment where everyone steps up to help where needed. This is a full-time role that requires on-site work, Monday - Friday for first 90 days. 



Responsibilities:

 - Solving hard problems. Owning complex technical cases: writing and debugging different coding languages, tracking down root-cause architectural issues across platforms, and navigating issues spanning multiple layers and different technologies.

 - Working directly with customers. Helping customers and system integrators by phone and email, whether they're technical or not, and keeping them informed while you work. 

 - Getting very good at root-cause analysis. Building diagnostic skills that will serve you for your whole career. 

 - Documenting as you go. Keeping clear records of ticket progress, issue breakdowns, and resolutions. They become the knowledgebase articles of tomorrow. 

 - Leaving your fingerprints on Ignition. Proposing enhancements, advocating for fixes, and partnering with Software Engineering to shape future releases. The more you master Ignition, the more your ideas drive the roadmap. 

 - Growing with the work. Level I is the start of a path through the Senior Software Solutions Engineer role, where you'll take on the toughest cases and help train the next engineers in. 

 - Getting Ignition Certified. Completing Core and Gold Ignition certifications funded by Inductive Automation before touching a live customer system. 



Requirements:

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience with SCADA systems, PLCs, or industrial control networks is required 

 - Comfort writing code (Java, Python, etc.) and SQL queries

 - Familiarity with relational databases (MS SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, etc.) and how tables relate 

 - Experience with Windows, Linux, and macOS; command line skills are a plus 

 - Comfort troubleshooting live alongside customers 

 - Confidence learning unfamiliar subjects on the fly 

 - Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to listen, acknowledge frustration, and steer a tense situation toward a solution 



Not required, but preferred:  

 - Customer Service experience 

 - Experience with PLCs (Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Omron, Siemens, etc.), HMIs, or industrial networks 

 - Experience with Ignition or other SCADA/HMI platforms
